# Appendix A: Non-Vacuity Witnesses {.unnumbered}

Both instances of @sec-instances carry the same four witnesses over
finite types, so that no theorem there is vacuously true of an empty
structure. Nothing in the body depends on reading them.

1. **A closed artifact.** An evidence snapshot supplying one admitted
 vouch and one admitted corroboration classifies the artifact
 $\lean{closed}$.
2. **A base-bounded $\lean{Total}$.** A single artifact closing directly onto
 the genesis seed satisfies $\lean{Total}$, which is what makes the
 minimality equality of @sec-instances non-empty.
3. **A defeated $\lean{Total}$.** The same shape with the evidence snapshot
 emptied fails $\lean{Total}$ through an $\lean{establishGap}$
, so $\lean{Total}$ is a real condition
 rather than one satisfied by construction.
4. **No vouchers, no $\lean{Total}$.** A policy admitting no vouchers forbids
 every non-seed $\lean{Total}$. This is the sharpest
 of the four: the accounting depends on admitted testimony, and does
 not derive everything from the gate.
